Far more serious: search "plumbers merchant near Shoreditch" and the result is cityplumbing.co.uk, a national chain describing itself as "the UK's largest builders' merchants" — the independent on Kingsland Road does not appear in the local pack at all, surfacing only via a scraped third-party directory. research.summary: Trade and retail counter, warehouse, and a genuine bathroom showroom at 51–55 Kingsland Road, Shoreditch E2, trading as City Plumbing since 1990 (the current entity, City Plumbing London Ltd, formerly City Plumbing Kingsland Limited, was incorporated 12 Aug 2011). Listed as a stockist by five separate premium suppliers — AXOR, hansgrohe, HiB, Press Tite and Ideal Bathrooms — this is a serious showroom, not just a parts counter. 4.8 stars from 89 Google reviews, the largest review base of any prospect researched across this whole pipeline, and £678,168 in shareholders' funds, by far the strongest balance sheet researched. A new Lloyds Bank charge was registered in February 2026, seven months before this research — a business actively borrowing and investing. Two directors, Parndip Singh (38) and Jagdip Singh (36), have run it since incorporation with zero resignations in fifteen years; either can almost certainly approve £400 alone. Despite all of this, they have no website, and the single biggest problem is a national chain called City Plumbing (cityplumbing.co.uk) that has taken over every search for their own trading name — the independent doesn't appear in the local pack at all for a search on its own name.

talkingPoints: Search City Plumbing and you get the national lot. You've been trading under that name since 1990 and they've taken it off you online. You've got nothing to fight back with.
Eighty-nine reviews at 4.8. That's more than any merchant I've looked at in London, and it lives in exactly one place.
AXOR and hansgrohe both list you as a stockist. That's good — except the customer does all their looking on hansgrohe's site, and you're one name on a list at the end of it.
You describe yourselves as the largest independent in London. That's a hell of a claim — where can anyone actually read it?
You're posting on Instagram already, so you clearly know it matters. Where does that link go? There's nowhere for it to point.
notes: REAL RESEARCH — sourced from Companies House, Google, Yell and supplier stockist pages (AXOR, hansgrohe, Press Tite, Ideal Bathrooms), compiled 11 Sep 2026, as part of a five-business batch. This is the strongest prospect of all eight businesses researched across the whole pipeline (Kenon, The Plumbing Merchant, MGM, and this batch of five) — call it first.

Ask for Parndip or Jagdip Singh — both directors since 2011, zero resignations, registered at the shop. Either can very likely approve £400 alone. No gatekeeper to navigate; if asked what it's about, say: "It's about how you come up on Google — the national City Plumbing is taking your searches."
Best time to call: Tuesday–Thursday 10:00–11:30, or 14:00–15:30. Avoid 07:00–09:00 (van rush) and lunch.
Before dialling: have the search result for their own name on screen, showing the national chain ranking above them. Screenshot it — you may be asked to send it within a minute.

Pitch this as fixing a search problem, not "a small website" — a business that calls itself London's largest independent may otherwise think a £400 site is beneath them. Frame it around the name-collision problem, not a generic website pitch.

Honest odds from the research: 8/10 chance of getting through, 6/10 of booking a meeting (the best of any prospect researched), 5/10 of closing — they have the money and a live, specific reason to act.
Never mention the £75/month or £50/month products on this call — a business that just took on a Lloyds facility doesn't need another subscription in the decision.

Two directors who may well be brothers (same correspondence address in Ilford) — "I'd have to ask my brother" is a plausible, genuine objection here, not a brush-off. Make it easy to pass on by offering to build the mockup first.

script.opening: Morning — is Parndip about? Or Jagdip? ... You don't know me, and I'll be straight with you — this is a cold call. Thirty seconds, and if it's no use I'll go away.
script.hook: I searched plumbers' merchants round Shoreditch this morning. What came up was cityplumbing.co.uk — the national chain. You weren't in the local results at all. You've traded as City Plumbing since 1990 and they've effectively taken the name off you online.
script.valueStatement: What I do is small and specific. One site: who you are, what you stock, the showroom, your reviews on it, and your own name pointing at you instead of at them. That's it — nothing you don't need.
script.demoOffer: Here's what I'd suggest. Separate from all that — half the sites listing you say you open at seven and one says nine. I'll get that corrected where I can, no charge, whether you want the site or not. On top of that, give me till Thursday and I'll build what your actual page would look like — your reviews, your brands, your name on it. Fifteen minutes, you look at the real thing, you tell me yes or no.
script.pricing: Four hundred pounds, once. Nothing monthly, no contract. You own it.

discovery.question: How long's the shop been on Kingsland Road?
discovery.why: Simple rapport opener while establishing who you're speaking to.
listenFor: Any long-tenure answer supports the "trading since 1990" claim from their own Google description

discovery.question: When a new customer comes in, where's he usually come from?
discovery.why: Sets up the name-collision angle directly — if search comes up, ask what they find when they look themselves up.
listenFor: Any mention of search or Google hands you straight into the hook

discovery.question: Do you do much bathroom work, or is it mostly parts?
discovery.why: Confirms the showroom side is real before leaning on the AXOR/hansgrohe angle.
listenFor: Any real showroom volume supports leading with the higher-value bathroom conversation

discovery.question: Do you ever get calls that clearly meant the chain?
discovery.why: Makes the name-collision problem concrete in his own words — he may already be irritated by this.
listenFor: Any "yeah, actually" is the value statement written for you

discovery.question: Anyone ever turned up when you were shut because a listing was wrong?
discovery.why: Makes the opening-hours inconsistency concrete without you having to lead with it.
listenFor: Any real anecdote here supports the free hours-correction offer

discovery.question: What's a decent bathroom job worth to you?
discovery.why: His own number becomes the ROI argument later — don't react to whatever he says, just note it.
listenFor: Any figure at all makes the £400 comparison trivial to make

extraObjections.objection: We've traded thirty years without one.
extraObjections.meaning: Never contradict the history — agree with it completely before making the point about what's changed.
extraObjections.response: And that's exactly why it's worth ten minutes — you've built something most places didn't survive to build. The bit that's changed isn't you, it's that the chain with your name now owns the search.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Suppose that's true. / Never thought about it that way.
extraObjections.followUp: Move straight to the name-collision demonstration if you haven't already shown it.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If he's adamant nothing needs to change, accept it — but the name-collision finding is hard to dismiss once seen.

extraObjections.objection: Our customers are trade, they don't browse.
extraObjections.meaning: True of the regulars, not true of the showroom customer.
extraObjections.response: The plumbers don't, you're right — they've got your number. But you've got a bathroom showroom. That customer's been on her phone for a month before she walks in anywhere.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Suppose there is a bit of that. / Not really, no.
extraObjections.followUp: If there's real showroom volume, move into the AXOR/hansgrohe angle directly.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If there's genuinely no showroom trade worth mentioning, fall back to the name-collision problem alone — it doesn't need the showroom angle to work.

extraObjections.objection: We get ten of you a week.
extraObjections.meaning: Fatigue with generic callers, not a rejection of this specific finding. Prove you're different, checkably.
extraObjections.response: I know, and they all open with "you haven't got a website". I opened with the fact that a national chain has taken your name in search. Type it in while I'm on the phone — I'll wait.
extraObjections.likelyReply: (He checks, and sees it.) / Didn't realise that.
extraObjections.followUp: Once he's seen it, move into the 89-reviews and showroom points.
extraObjections.whenToStop: Only offer this if you're confident the search result is still current — check before the call, not during it.

extraObjections.objection: Who else have you built for?
extraObjections.meaning: A reference check. Never invent a client — a fabricated reference is fatal if checked.
extraObjections.response: Straight answer — I'm building this up, so you'd be an early one, and that's exactly why you'd get proper attention rather than being file number forty. Judge me on the work: let me build yours and show you first.
extraObjections.likelyReply: Fair enough. / I'd rather see something first.
extraObjections.followUp: Move straight to the demo offer — the work is the reference.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If he insists on existing client work you don't have, be honest rather than stretching the truth.

extraObjections.objection: How do I know you'll still be around?
extraObjections.meaning: A fair question about risk, not hostility.
extraObjections.response: Fair question. It's a one-off, so you're not tied to me monthly, and the site's yours — domain, files, the lot. If I vanished tomorrow any developer could pick it up. That's deliberate.
extraObjections.followUp: Move to the demo offer — showing the actual page builds more trust than more words.
extraObjections.whenToStop: If he remains unconvinced, offer to send the example anyway rather than over-arguing it.

extraObjections.meaning: A pre-emptive objection to something you weren't suggesting — agree immediately.
extraObjections.response: Nor would I in your line. Not suggesting it — this is just so the people already searching for you find you rather than the chain.
extraObjections.followUp: Return to the name-collision point immediately.
extraObjections.whenToStop: N/A — should resolve in one line.

extraObjections.meaning: A comparison on the wrong axis — service and knowledge are where they actually win.
extraObjections.response: You can't and you shouldn't. Nobody reviews Screwfix saying the staff really knew their stuff. Eighty-nine people said that about you.
extraObjections.followUp: Move to the 4.8/89 reviews point if it hasn't landed yet.
extraObjections.whenToStop: N/A — this should redirect the conversation, not end it.
